title: Higher-order smoothness only at the lower level: joint gradients and a mean-square target
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

feedback_quality.description: Conditional on the pre-call history H, each block's expectation equals the corresponding population partial gradient. The sum of conditional expected squared errors over the four blocks is at most sigma², which is at most M².

bounds.derivation: The source Theorem 3.1 bounds mean-square error by $C(\Delta_0/K+\tau^{2p}+1/(m\tau^2))$. Here $K$ is the outer iteration count, $m$ the batch size, $\tau$ the perturbation scale, and $\Delta_0$ the initial potential gap. Choose $\tau\asymp\varepsilon^{1/p}$, $m\asymp\varepsilon^{-2}\tau^{-2}$, and $K\asymp\Delta_0\varepsilon^{-2}$ so that each term has the target squared-error order.
